calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Blues are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Devils’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.7 expected goals per 60 against the Blues.

calls.happened: On the power play, New Jersey had 9.3 expected goals per 60 tonight, against a league average of 7.7 expected goals per 60. They usually sit at 8.8 expected goals per 60.

calls.title: The chances came, the goals didn’t
calls.plain: The Devils beat the league average on the power play, even against the Blues. They didn’t score on it, though: 0 for 3.
calls.said: the Devils’ power play would win the standoff with the Blues’ kill

calls.head: Like for like: Mantha vs. Buchnevich
calls.body: At home, the Devils keep sending Mantha’s line (Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Sheldon Keefe keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Blues’ third line is Neighbours, Dvorský and Buchnevich.
calls.call: The Devils’ L3 (Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist) spends at least 34% of its 5-on-5 time against the Blues’ third line, against about 22% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 45% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 22% with no line matching
calls.cite: Matchups · New Jersey home games this season · 9 games, 45 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: New Jersey’s L3 (Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist) at home: 45% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ third lines. Matchups, New Jersey home games this season, 9 games, 45 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face third lines about 22% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: New Jersey’s L3 (Mantha, Rodrigues, Boqvist) spent 15% of its 5-on-5 time against St. Louis’s L3 (1:30 of 10:13). The call needed 34%, halfway from the 22% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 45%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist barely saw the Blues’ third line
calls.plain: New Jersey sent Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist out against the Blues’ third line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Keefe sent them out against Toropchenko, Suter and Johnston (4:18 of 10:13 at 5-on-5).
calls.said: Sheldon Keefe would send Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist out against the Blues’ third line again

calls.head: Binnington doesn’t own the Devils
calls.body: Binnington has been a wall against the Devils since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Binnington isn’t that wall tonight.
calls.call: If Binnington starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .898 than to his .935 against the Devils.

STL.head: We gave St. Louis only a 34% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Devils blow a three-goal lead, then win it in overtime
paras: Luke Hughes struck first for the Devils early in the first. The second period was a wild one. Jake Neighbours and Timo Meier fought early in the period, and Anthony Mantha made it 2-0 for the Devils midway through the period. Robert Thomas got the Blues on the board on the power play just over four minutes later. Jesper Boqvist and Mantha scored just 19 seconds apart later in the period to push the lead to 4-1. Mason McTavish, Philip Broberg and Dalibor Dvorský scored three goals in just over three minutes midway through the third to tie it 4-4. Jesper Bratt won it a minute and a half into overtime. Mantha added an assist for a three-point night.

The Devils had a bit more of the good stuff. Connor Hellebuyck made 28 saves for the Devils, and Jordan Binnington stopped 31 of 36 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Jack Hughes, even with Bratt’s overtime winner in the game, by our Swing measure. The Devils moved to 11-5-0, second in the Metropolitan, while the Blues dropped to 7-7-2, sixth in the Central.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Devils.
The Devils have beaten the Blues four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
One of the preview’s three calls held.
